cases.prompt: A membrane-protein mutant reaches the cell surface at normal abundance but abolishes solute flux. Design the shortest evidence chain that distinguishes loss of pore function from loss of protein delivery, and state one remaining alternative explanation.

rubric.criterion: Uses a direct localization/abundance control
Measures transport with matched expression and a suitable negative control
Names an alternative such as altered gating, selectivity, membrane potential, or cell viability

limitations: This preserved three-criterion checklist is self-assessment, not an analytic grading rubric or an institutional grade.

cases.prompt: Integrative project milestone 1 (suggested week 10). Using form A of the project culture table, write a 150–250-word question and scope note. State one question the measurements can answer, the principal comparison among control, signal_high, matrix_high and both, the independent unit, and the deliberate cell-number and matrix-presentation limitations. Add a short data dictionary in your own words.

rubric.criterion: My question can be answered with named comparisons, measurement layers and units, and it is bounded to this synthetic in-vitro model.
I name the independently prepared culture as the unit and treat cells, aliquots and the two endpoint times as measurements within a culture.
I identify the principal two-by-two comparison (control, signal_high, matrix_high, both) and keep signal_low and rescue as separate comparisons.
I name the unequal viable-cell numbers and the matrix_high modulus/ligand confound as built-in limitations.
I make no clinical, therapeutic or mechanistic claim that this design cannot support.

limitations: Optional self-check for the integrative project. The response is saved privately and is never submitted, scored or graded; the separate inactive project candidate and its human rubric remain unreviewed.

cases.prompt: Integrative project milestone 2 (suggested week 11). Write a reproducible analysis plan for form A: list every transformation and its order, the denominators, how cultures and times are handled, the controls present and absent, and at least two competing explanations with the readout that would separate them.

rubric.criterion: Each transformation has a formula and an order: background subtraction, spike or protein recovery correction, then normalization per 1000 viable cells.
I compute per-culture quantities before equal-culture condition means, and I use one signaling trajectory per culture without counting the repeated columns twice.
I list the controls that are present and the controls that are absent.
I give at least two competing explanations and the readout that would distinguish them.
I separate descriptive calculations from any inferential or causal model and state that these deterministic values do not support p-values.

limitations: Optional self-check for the integrative project. The response is saved privately and is never submitted, scored or graded; the separate inactive project candidate and its human rubric remain unreviewed.

cases.prompt: Integrative project milestone 3 (suggested week 13). Paste your form-A condition summary table as text and the text alternative for your figure. Keep your full per-culture CSV and figure file yourself; the Case studio stores text only.

rubric.criterion: My working table has one row per culture and time, and my condition summary uses equal-culture means.
Marker and function percentages use the viable-cell denominator, and every RNA, protein and pERK-area value carries its unit.
I show culture-level spread descriptively and do not present it as an inferential interval.
My figure is labelled, and its text alternative states the comparison, the pattern and its limits; the table gives the same numbers.
I checked my transformation steps against the open rehearsal practice before applying them to form A.

limitations: Optional self-check for the integrative project. The response is saved privately and is never submitted, scored or graded; the separate inactive project candidate and its human rubric remain unreviewed.

cases.prompt: Integrative project milestone 4 (suggested week 14). Write a 400–700-word evidence interpretation that separates molecular, signaling, cell-marker and function-proxy claims, then design one factorial follow-up and state which result would distinguish your alternatives.

rubric.criterion: I keep RNA quantity, recovered protein, signaling area, marker percentage and the function proxy as separate claims.
I state at least two alternative explanations, including the ligand/modulus confound, viable-cell loss and the missing joint marker-function states.
My follow-up matches accessible ligand, measures material properties, uses independent cultures, includes positive and negative controls, and measures marker and function separately.
I state which result would distinguish the alternatives.
I state what this synthetic experiment cannot establish, including any clinical benefit.

rubric.criterion: I name the form, the file, the independent unit, every formula, the rounding rule and any exclusions.
Someone else could reproduce my tables and figure from this note alone.
